placements.name: Lila
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Lila proved to be a steady and well-connected competitor in The Circle 1, placing 1 as the winner, becoming an Influencer 3 times, and making 2 blocks. She played through overlapping alliances with Barbie, Derek, Elijah, Hector, Luis, Mateo, Domingo, Sasha, Curtis, Dr.Ines, Lorraine, and Wyatt, while also developing a showmance with Luis. Despite an early private plan forming against her, she remained valuable to other players, later learning during Mateo's visit that she had been talking to two siblings behind one profile. In the finale, the room celebrated her win after she beat Sasha.
placements.personality: Lila came across as warm and measured, often offering simple reassurance rather than over-explaining herself. She could be quietly pointed when she needed to be, leaving a chat before Hector could answer or smiling slowly at the screen when she sensed fear around her. Her connections were personal as much as strategic, especially with Sasha and Luis, but she usually kept her tone calm even when the game around her got messy.

quotes.text: It's still me. It's just me on a really, really good day.
Loyalty goes both ways
Sasha, thank you for being exactly who you said you were

trivia: Lila was seen holding a cucumber slice in place with one hand while typing with the other.
Dr.Ines described Lila as "so brave in the chat."
She told the group she and Mateo were "absolutely not a thing" before his visit revealed the shared profile.

placements.name: Sasha
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Sasha proved to be a major endgame force in The Circle 1, placing 2 as a finalist, becoming an Influencer 3 times, and making 3 blocks. She played in alliances with Derek, Lila, Barbie, Hector, Domingo, Curtis, Elijah, Wyatt, and Sasha's key rivals Anais, Domingo, and Dr.Ines shaped much of her path. She protected Nadiya, argued that Barbie was running the game, and later pushed the case that Domingo was like the final boss. In the finale, she remained close to Derek after his reveal and ultimately lost to Lila.
placements.personality: Sasha was funny, nervous, and openly dramatic, turning pressure into jokes about counters, paper airplanes, and rankings that were "basically top if you squint." She attached strongly to people she trusted, especially Brooke, while still watching timing and posts closely enough to suspect when something was too convenient. As the game tightened, her humor stayed intact, but she became more direct about needing security.

quotes.text: Circle, change my job. Nobody needs to know what I actually do for a living. Not in here.
Mateo goes last! I tried once! It didn't land! Like a paper airplane in the rain!
I wanted fireworks and I got a sparkler.

trivia: Sasha almost signed off with her real name early in the season.
She admitted she had wiped the counter six times while waiting.
After one screen moment, she gave the screen a standing ovation while alone in her apartment.

placements.name: Derek
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Derek played the whole season as the catfish profile "Brooke" and placed 3 as a finalist in The Circle 1. He became an Influencer 3 times, made 2 blocks, and played through alliances with Lila, Sasha, Barbie, Hector, Domingo, Curtis, Elijah, Wyatt, Luis, Mateo, and Dr.Ines. As Brooke, he built enough trust to become central to several players' games while hiding that the face and name were false. At the finale, Derek revealed he had been Brooke all along, and Sasha still called him her person.
placements.personality: Derek's Brooke was soft, intimate, and strategic, often using vulnerability to keep people close while quietly calculating survival. Alone, Derek was much more anxious and self-aware, questioning whether he had been "the bad guy" and admitting he was not ready for people to see him. He also had a fussy, contained apartment energy, from straightening cushions to not looking up from his nails.
trivia: Derek played as Brooke for the entire season.
He straightened the cushions for the third time during one tense stretch.
He once actually put both hands up while alone in the apartment.

quotes.text: Brooke is sweet, Brooke is fun, and Brooke is never, ever gonna get caught.
Was I the bad guy just now? I think I was the bad guy.
I'm not ready for Jace to see me. I'm not ready.

placements.name: Barbie
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Barbie placed 4 as a finalist in The Circle 1 and became one of the season's most watched social players. She played in alliances with Lila, Derek, Elijah, Hector, Luis, Mateo, Domingo, Sasha, Curtis, Dr.Ines, Lorraine, and Wyatt, and she also had a showmance with Wyatt. After entering, she watched the group before fully joining it, bonded with Lila, grew close to Brooke, and was later accused by Sasha of running the game. At the finale, she embraced both Derek and Elijah after their catfish reveals.
placements.personality: Barbie was observant before she was expressive, literally pulling a chair up to the screen to study the group before committing herself. Once she chose people, she could be very affectionate, sending hearts, saying talking to someone was the best part of her day, and reacting physically with hands to her heart or head in her hands. She also kept a strategic edge, noting when Kad was becoming popular and telling herself to keep things light.

quotes.text: They don't know I'm watching. Circle, show me the chat. Let's see who's who.
Keep it light. Keep them guessing.
I'm dancing so badly. I'm having the best time.

trivia: Barbie pulled a chair right up to the screen when she first watched the group.
She said she had run out of things to do in her apartment.
She once fell back on the bed laughing after a chat.

placements.name: Elijah
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Elijah played the whole season as the catfish profile "Kad" and placed 5 as a finalist in The Circle 1. He became an Influencer 1 time, made 1 block, and played in alliances with Lila, Derek, Barbie, Hector, Luis, Mateo, Domingo, Dr.Ines, Sasha, Wyatt, and Lorraine. His identity came under direct suspicion when Lorraine's goodbye video revealed Jace was a catfish and warned everyone that Kad was one too. At the finale, Elijah revealed that he had played Kad using his cousin's photos, and Barbie embraced him after the reveal.
placements.personality: Elijah's Kad was loud, eager, and reactive, with all-caps excitement that made even small wins feel huge. He wanted to be friendly and fun, but he was also easily rattled by suspicion, staring at punctuation or freezing mid-bite when his name came up. By the end, that nervous energy turned sharper, especially when he felt Barbie had been coming for him.
trivia: Elijah played as Kad using his cousin's photos.
He once froze with a spoon halfway to his mouth after hearing his name.
He described Brooke's style as not small talk but "medium talk."

quotes.text: New kid energy. Be friendly. Be fun. Don't trust anybody yet.
Did Jace just say my NAME?! On the way OUT?!
BARBIE HAS BEEN COMING FOR ME ALL WEEK! I'M DONE!

placements.name: Hector
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Hector played the whole season as the catfish profile "Nadiya" and placed 6 after being blocked in The Circle 1. He became an Influencer 5 times, made 4 blocks, and played in alliances with Lila, Derek, Barbie, Elijah, Luis, Mateo, Domingo, Sasha, Curtis, Lorraine, Wyatt, and Hector's rival Ruth. His Nadiya profile stayed powerful deep into the game, while he carefully maintained the character and navigated rivalries with Domingo and Ruth. His run ended when he was voted out in episode 13.
placements.personality: Hector was meticulous about playing Nadiya, keeping notes on age, job, and hometown and reminding himself to stay in character. He could be warm and flirty in messages, but alone he was controlled and tense, rereading chats, pacing, and rehearsing what Nadiya would say. When cornered, his instinct was discipline rather than panic, though the apartment footage showed how much effort that discipline took.
trivia: Hector kept a folded piece of paper with him while playing Nadiya.
He turned a lamp off and then back on during one tense night.
He described Barbie withholding support as a reason she would not get his help.

quotes.text: I have my notes. Age, job, hometown. If I slip once, I'm done. So I don't slip.
Stay in character. What would Nadiya actually say here?
If that door opens, Domingo is gonna see someone he has never seen before.

placements.name: Luis
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Luis shared the profile "Mateo" with Mateo, with messages from that profile written by both of them, and placed 7 after being blocked in The Circle 1. He played in an alliance with Barbie, Lila, Derek, Elijah, Hector, Mateo, and Domingo, and the shared profile also developed a showmance with Lila. As the game progressed, Luis and Mateo struggled to keep one voice behind Mateo, arguing over wording and how the profile should sound. Their run ended in episode 12, when they were blocked and revealed that the players had been talking to two people the whole time.
placements.personality: Luis was the more cautious and editorial half of the shared Mateo profile, constantly worrying that the wrong wording would expose them. He pushed for shorter, safer messages, objected to hearts, and corrected lines that sounded too strange. His banter with Mateo was affectionate but exasperated, full of whispered arguments and sibling impatience.
trivia: Luis and Mateo wrestled for the remote like it was the last cookie.
He worried that their mother would be disappointed by one of their messages.
In their goodbye video, Luis and Mateo pointed out that they never said "we" once.

quotes.text: If we say that, they'll know it's two people.
quotes.context: while arguing over the Mateo profile

quotes.text: No hearts. Hearts are how you get blocked.
We ARE weird. That's the brand.

placements.name: Mateo
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Mateo shared the profile "Mateo" with Luis, with messages from that profile written by both of them, and placed 7 after being blocked in The Circle 1. He entered with Luis behind the profile, played in an alliance with Barbie, Lila, Derek, Elijah, Hector, Luis, and Domingo, and developed a showmance with Lila. The pair struggled to keep one voice, but Mateo refused to move against Lila when Nadiya tried to build a group that could run the game. After being blocked in episode 12, Mateo chose to visit Lila, revealing in person that she had been speaking to two siblings.
placements.personality: Mateo was the more openly emotional and enthusiastic half of the shared profile, arriving as a fan who had watched the show and then immediately feeling the pressure of being inside it. He was playful and self-conscious, covering his face with a pillow, panic-joking about ratings, and noticing small things like whether Sasha actually laughed. Compared with Luis, he was more likely to want the message to sound natural and personal, even when that made the profile harder to control.
trivia: Mateo scrolled back to see every answer after entering.
He covered his face with a pillow more than once during stressful or funny moments.
He took the stairs one at a time on the way to visit Lila.

quotes.text: I've watched this show a hundred times. Now it's me.
I'm down there. Okay. Okay. Nobody panic. Especially me.
Circle, just tell me. I can't take the dots.

placements.name: Domingo
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Domingo placed 9 after being blocked in The Circle 1, became an Influencer 2 times, and made 2 blocks. He played in alliances with Lila, Derek, Barbie, Elijah, Hector, Luis, Mateo, Sasha, Curtis, Dr.Ines, and Lorraine, while also having a showmance with Dr.Ines and rivalries with Anais, Hector, and Sasha. He built personal connections, steered decisions around Anais, and was later described by Sasha as like the final boss. His run ended when he was voted out in episode 11.
placements.personality: Domingo mixed charm with calculation, blowing kisses at the screen while also looking for the safest social position and writing question marks next to names. He liked real conversations and pushed others to be sincere, but he was also willing to name dangerous players and make the strategic case plainly. His flirtier, more intimate side came through with Dr.Ines and Barbie, though he often kept one foot in analysis.

quotes.text: Near the top and not an Influencer. Perfect. That's the sweet spot.
Post something real. Just once.
The person being blocked is playing this game better than any of us

trivia: Domingo once opened a private chat and then closed it again.
He wrote a question mark next to a name while sorting through suspicions.
He described Barbie as someone he had talked to about "everything in here."

placements.name: Lorraine
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Lorraine played the whole season as the catfish profile "Jace" and placed 10 after being blocked in The Circle 1. She played in an alliance with Elijah, Lila, Barbie, Hector, and Domingo. After entering as Jace, she connected loudly and enthusiastically, but her own visit revealed that neither she nor Elijah looked like their profiles. Her goodbye video confirmed Jace was a catfish and warned everyone that Kad was one too.
placements.personality: Lorraine was energetic, loud, and openly delighted to be in The Circle, announcing herself, dancing in the doorway, and turning chats into all-caps bursts. As Jace, she tried to be social through humor, snacks, and big reactions, but she could also switch into game mode and make a head-over-heart decision. Near the end, the excitement gave way to nerves, with pacing and mirror checks before the reveal.
trivia: Lorraine played as Jace for her entire time in The Circle.
She turned the volume all the way up during one episode.
Before her face-to-face reveal, she checked her hair in the mirror twice.

quotes.text: 'A new Player has entered the Circle.' That's me! That's me!
My neighbors can probably hear me
Hey, Circle. I'm Lorraine, not Jace. But Jace is waiting at home, and Jace is really cool.

placements.name: Dr.Ines
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Dr.Ines placed 11 after being blocked in The Circle 1. She played in an alliance with Domingo, Lila, Derek, Barbie, and Elijah, developed a showmance with Domingo, and had a rivalry with Sasha. After entering, she tried to find support ahead of the ratings and leaned into a close connection with Domingo. Her run ended when she was voted out in episode 8.
placements.personality: Dr.Ines was anxious, apologetic, and hesitant in the chat, often beginning with "um" and worrying that she had talked too much. Her messages tended to soften every request, even when she was directly asking for protection. She still had flashes of excitement and flirtation, laughing into a pillow, doing a lap of the living room, and giving Domingo more confidence when the connection felt real.
trivia: Dr.Ines frequently used ellipses and "um" in her messages.
She wrote a name on a notepad and underlined it.
A nap changed her life, according to one of her updates.

quotes.text: honestly I'm so nervous. This helps a lot...
okay, I'll go. Sorry if I talked too much...
Dots, dots, dots. I hate dots.

placements.name: Wyatt
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Wyatt placed 12 after being blocked in The Circle 1 and became an Influencer 1 time. He played in an alliance with Hector, Lila, Sasha, Derek, Barbie, and Elijah, and he developed a showmance with Anais. Early on, he noticed enough to know that a private plan against Lila existed, and he was openly suspicious of Sasha. His run ended when he was voted out in episode 5.
placements.personality: Wyatt was guarded and analytical, changing details on his profile so people would not treat him differently and doing crosswords while watching the game. He could be blunt in ratings and suspicion, especially toward Sasha, but he also softened quickly in flirtation with Anais and Nadiya. His confidence often came out as dry understatement, like calling his flirting "just a little bit."

quotes.text: If they knew the real number, they'd treat me differently. So the number changes.
Sasha is a catfish. I'd bet on it. Last.
Just a little bit of flirting. A little.

trivia: Wyatt was doing a crossword at the kitchen counter when first seen.
He and Anais sat facing each other with their knees almost touching.
He told a departing player that their apartment was exactly like his, except with snacks.

placements.name: Anais
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Anais placed 13 after being blocked in The Circle 1. She developed a showmance with Wyatt and had rivalries with Domingo and Sasha. After entering, she tried to build sincere connections, grew close enough to Wyatt for a real face-to-face moment, and left a goodbye video confirming that her pictures were real. Her run ended when she was voted out in episode 4.
placements.personality: Anais was earnest, romantic, and easily overwhelmed by the emotional side of The Circle. She asked simple getting-to-know-you questions, worried about hurting people, and wanted one real moment before leaving. Her connection with Wyatt stood out because she dropped the game tone entirely when they met in person.

quotes.text: 'A new Player has entered the Circle.' That's me! That's me!
If I'm leaving, I'm leaving with one real moment.
Hey, Circle! It's Anais. Yes, those were my real pictures. Just my good-lighting pictures.

trivia: Anais did a little dance in the doorway when she entered.
She asked players whether they were morning people or night people.
Anais and Wyatt kissed during her visit, and neither looked at the cameras.

placements.name: Curtis
placements.lead: During his time on the show, Curtis placed 14 after being blocked in The Circle 1. He played in an alliance with Derek, Lila, Sasha, Barbie, Hector, and Domingo. He entered cautiously, avoiding party pictures because he did not want to seem like a threat, and built friendly early ties, including a crush on Brooke. His run ended when he was voted out in episode 3.
placements.personality: Curtis was cautious, agreeable, and eager to be liked, often choosing middle ground until he knew where people stood. He responded warmly to attention, blushing at compliments and taking Brooke's support seriously. When his closest connection was in danger, though, he framed loyalty simply: ride or die meant he would go.

quotes.text: I'm not using the party pictures. I don't want anyone seeing me as a threat on day one.
People like me. People actually like me.
Ride or die means ride or die. I go.

trivia: Curtis had a crush on Brooke.
He pulled a blanket around his shoulders during one early moment.
Anais and Curtis hugged in the doorway after his blocking.

placements.name: Ruth
placements.lead: During her time on the show, Ruth placed 15 after being blocked in The Circle 1. She had a rivalry with Hector and quickly tried to build numbers against Lila. Her early game was direct, practical, and openly strategic, including a plan to put Lila at the bottom. Her run ended when she was voted out in episode 2.
placements.personality: Ruth was blunt, transactional, and funny in a dry way, treating The Circle like business but not pretending it felt good. She was willing to target Lila immediately and say she was being careful rather than scared. In person, her hard edge softened, as she admitted she had come to scream and ended up wanting to hug.

quotes.text: Everything on this profile is true. Almost everything. Circle, save it before I change my mind.
if the three of us put lila at the bottom, lila is in trouble
I came here to scream at you, and now I kind of want to hug you. I hate this place.
quotes.context: during her visit after being blocked

trivia: Ruth admitted she had eaten all the good snacks on day one.
She cracked her knuckles in the hallway before her visit.
She and Derek both laughed a little too loud after she was blocked.

twists.name: Ride or Die
twists.desc: Secret compatibility answers pair every player with a Ride or Die. It lasts for one Ratings and one blocking. At the Ratings, the top-rated player's partner becomes the second Influencer, wherever they were rated. At the blocking, once the name is announced, the blocked player's partner can choose to go home in their place. Players learn who their own partner is and nobody else's, so that blocking is also a question of who would take the fall for whom.

twists.name: A Date With One of Three
twists.desc: The Circle shows the newcomer three players and tells them to take one on a virtual dinner date and send them a gift. The newcomer picks, the date happens in a private chat, and the gift arrives at the chosen player's door. The whole building hears who was picked, and the two who were offered and passed over feel it.

twists.name: The Newcomer Throws a Party
twists.desc: The newcomer has to throw a party on their first night and choose who is invited. About half the building gets a message and a good time, and a first bond with the host. The other half sees the party happening without them, and every one of them notices exactly who was left out, including themselves.

twists.name: Arrive as a Pair
twists.desc: Two newcomers arrive on the same night, and before either meets anyone else the Circle puts them in a private chat with each other. They walk into the building already knowing one person, and usually already allied: two new votes that can move together from day one.

twists.name: Save Then Plead
twists.desc: The two Influencers take turns saving players in public until only two are left. Those two then have to plead their case to the Influencers face to face on video, and a good plea can change a mind that seemed made up. The Influencers go to the Hangout and choose between the two; the other one is safe. The blocked player gets to meet one person before they leave.

twists.name: America's Block
twists.desc: Everyone rates as usual and the top two become Influencers, but tonight they do not block anybody: in the Hangout they nominate two players instead. The audience at home then votes to save one of the two, by who they have liked watching, and the live vote is shown on screen with the share each one got. The player with the smaller share is blocked, and both nominees know the Influencers put them there.

twists.name: Secret Influencers
twists.desc: Everyone rates as usual, but tonight nobody is shown the results: not their own place, and not who came top. The two top-rated players are told privately that they are the Influencers, and they meet in the Hangout without anyone else knowing it is them. The Circle announces the blocked name, not who chose it, so the whole building spends the next day guessing, and the blocked player has no idea whose door to knock on. They still get to meet one person before they leave.

gameHistory.title: Profiles and first ratings
gameHistory.prose: The original players entered The Circle and set up a mix of honest profiles, polished versions of themselves, and outright catfish, with Derek playing as Brooke and Hector playing as Nadiya. Early chats were cautious, with Brooke probing Curtis, Nadiya working quickly to get close to Domingo, and Ruth, Wyatt, and others testing where they stood. A private plan formed against Lila, while Wyatt noticed enough to know a plan existed. The game For Real For Real gave the players their first chance to read each other under pressure and left several of them, especially Ruth and Nadiya, with new suspicions. In the first ratings, players balanced genuine connections against threat management, and Nadiya ended the round with power.

gameHistory.title: Ruth goes home
gameHistory.prose: With Brooke and Nadiya in power, the Influencers treated the first blocking as a strategic move rather than a personal one. Brooke argued that Ruth was too well liked to keep, and Nadiya accepted that somebody had to take the blame for removing a social threat. Ruth was blocked, then left with a goodbye message that admitted some details of her profile were changed and warned the others about Brooke. Brooke immediately tried to control the damage by claiming Nadiya was not on the others' side, while Nadiya began worrying about where Wyatt fit into the fallout. Anais entered as a new player, Nadiya tried to reach her first, and the rest of the round was shaped by awards, flirting, suspicion of Nadiya, and another tense set of ratings.

gameHistory.title: Curtis leaves quietly
gameHistory.prose: The block was framed around strong social players and who could become loyal afterward, with Lila discussed as someone worth keeping. Curtis was blocked, despite several players fearing that Brooke or another visible threat could be the target. His goodbye video confirmed he had played as himself with his best side forward, and he specifically told Brooke he wanted her in the final. Brooke took Curtis's exit hard, posting about trying to stay positive while also keeping track of who had held power. Barbie then entered, watched the group before fully joining it, and the next ratings showed Brooke that she still had people willing to back her.

gameHistory.title: Anais is targeted
gameHistory.prose: Sasha pushed to protect Nadiya and argued that Wyatt was not worth using a block on, but Domingo steered the decision toward Anais. Anais was blocked because she was seen as one of the strongest players in the game, and Domingo accepted that he had made a winning move rather than a friendly one. Anais's goodbye video confirmed she was real, thanked Sasha, and warned everyone to watch Domingo. Dr.Ines entered afterward and immediately had to work out where she fit into an already connected group. The round settled into new one-on-one chats, suspicion around Nadiya, Barbie bonding with Lila, and ratings in which several players used the bottom spot to target people they saw as threats or unknowns.

gameHistory.title: Wyatt is exposed
gameHistory.prose: Lila opened the blocking discussion by naming Brooke as a dangerous front-runner, but Nadiya pushed the idea that Wyatt would be unsafe to leave in power. Wyatt was blocked, with the public explanation again focusing on a player being too loved and too dangerous to keep. He chose to visit Barbie before leaving, then revealed in his goodbye video that his face and name were real but some details were kept back. Wyatt also warned everyone to watch Nadiya, leaving Hector guilty because Nadiya had helped send him out. Kad and Jace then entered as new catfish profiles, and the round shifted into fresh flirting, a roast, and a party where old suspicions mixed with new connections.

gameHistory.title: Risky answers linger
gameHistory.prose: The players tried to reset after a rough night with status updates and morning chat, but even harmless messages were read for possible digs. Jace struggled to get traction in one-on-one conversation, while Dr.Ines grew closer to Domingo but noticed when he dodged a question. Kad created The Boys with Jace and Domingo, keeping the tone light before warning them to watch Lila. Risky Quizness put the players' past choices on display, and Lila's answers stood out enough that both Dr.Ines and Brooke kept thinking about them. A later party briefly lifted the mood, though Dr.Ines admitted she was having a hard day and Nadiya found the sudden kindness suspicious.

gameHistory.title: Inner Circle forms
gameHistory.prose: Brooke, Domingo, and Barbie all posted vulnerable status updates, and Nadiya enjoyed being near the top of the Newsfeed. Domingo continued building personal connections, including a flirtier bond, while Brooke directly asked Barbie if she had her top spot and treated the answer as a survival vote. Jace kept trying to entertain and connect, Sasha flirted openly, and Dr.Ines asked for support ahead of the ratings. Kad created The Inner Circle and tried to set up a structure where others would compete for influence inside it. The ratings left Dr.Ines at the bottom, shocking one apartment into a scream and another into silence.

gameHistory.title: Dr.Ines is blocked
gameHistory.prose: After the ratings, Sasha used the blocking discussion to argue that Barbie was running the game, while others tried to protect their own relationships. Dr.Ines was blocked because the Influencers said they could not shake the feeling that she was not who she claimed to be. Her goodbye video admitted that her listed job was not exactly true, thanked Domingo for making the game feel like home, and warned that somebody in the Circle was lying. Mateo entered with Luis behind the profile, immediately shifting attention as a new vote and a new possible ally. The round ended with Circle Scenarios, a failed push to put Domingo at the bottom, and ratings that made Brooke an Influencer.

gameHistory.title: Jace is revealed
gameHistory.prose: Brooke used her power to protect Nadiya and Sasha while arguing that Jace needed to go. Lorraine was blocked as Jace, accepted that being herself through the profile had not been enough, and chose to visit Kad. When she arrived, both Lorraine and Elijah realized neither of them looked like their profile, and Lorraine's goodbye video revealed Jace was a catfish while warning everyone that Kad was one too. Kad tried to redirect the warning by claiming his visit had warned him about Lila and Brooke, while the remaining players processed the loss through status posts and private chats. A gift exchange and party followed, but the night still carried paranoia about who was protecting whom and who was lying.

gameHistory.title: Alliance breaks down
gameHistory.prose: Nadiya thanked Sasha for her support during Night of Endless Heartbreak and proposed that they officially stick together. Brooke kept working her social ties, while Mateo and Luis struggled to keep one voice behind their profile and openly argued over how Mateo should sound. Nadiya tried to build a group that could run the game, but Mateo refused to move against Lila, showing that the alliance would not be simple. In the ratings, several players placed Mateo at the bottom, while Kad and Brooke continued targeting each other as threats. Afterward, The Inner Circle voted Nadiya out of her own alliance, and Brooke warned Sasha that some players had ended up much lower than they should have.

gameHistory.title: Domingo becomes target
gameHistory.prose: Nadiya and Sasha handled the blocking, with Nadiya wanting to keep Brooke useful and refusing to consider Lila. Sasha argued that Domingo was like the final boss and that a universally liked player had to be removed. Nadiya chose not to fight her and Domingo was blocked. His goodbye video confirmed he was real, warned that somebody was lying, and specifically told the others to watch Sasha. The rest of the round moved through emotional posts, renewed chats, the Batter Up pancake challenge, a party, family messages, and ratings where players knew the next Influencers could be anyone.

gameHistory.title: Mateo was two
gameHistory.prose: The blocking conversation cleared Sasha quickly, and the players moved toward removing Mateo. Luis and Mateo were blocked, ending their shared run behind the Mateo profile. Mateo chose to visit Lila, where she learned in person that she had been talking to two siblings, and their goodbye video revealed the same to everyone. After the reveal, Brooke quietly missed Mateo, Sasha sought new security, Kad tried to formalize teams, and Nadiya admitted she liked Kad beyond the game. The ratings that followed were the most openly endgame-focused yet, with Brooke putting Barbie first, Sasha trusting Brooke, and Kad putting Sasha last because everybody loved her.

gameHistory.title: Nadiya unmasked
gameHistory.prose: Brooke and Kad entered the blocking discussion with different targets, as Brooke argued strategically for Nadiya while Kad was angry at Barbie. Kad eventually announced that Nadiya was being blocked because she was too strong to face in the final, and Hector was blocked. Hector felt betrayed by people he had trusted, especially Brooke, and apologized during his final visit before revealing that Nadiya had been played with a family member's photos. His goodbye video told the truth, promised Lila coffee outside the game, and warned everyone that Brooke was not who they thought. Brooke then tried to repair the damage one person at a time before the final ratings, while Kad pushed The Fam to rate Brooke low and the finalists made their last strategic choices.

gameHistory.title: Final face reveal
gameHistory.prose: The finalists sent their last messages to The Circle, with Lila thanking the game for Sasha, Sasha saying she was leaving with Brooke, Kad admitting to Lila that only the face had been false, and Brooke confessing fear that Sasha would soon learn the truth. They left their apartments one by one and met face to face, where Elijah revealed he had played Kad using his cousin's photos and Derek revealed he had been Brooke all along. The finalists reacted with shock, but Sasha still called Derek her person, Lila accepted that his messages had been real, and Barbie embraced both Derek and Elijah. The blocked players then joined them, leading to reunions, apologies, and jokes about the lies everyone had told. The finale ended with the room celebrating Lila's win, while she thanked her family and told Sasha she loved her.
